clue.text: Creator of 10 computer games keeping quiet about animated character

parts.note: 10 across is ODYSSEY, the epic poem composed by Homer

indicators.note: the games hold the quiet sign within them, as a container keeps something

parts.note: The Sims is a famous series of computer games
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
on means about or concerning, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A games designer is pictured adding a quiet character to a cartoon, with a nod to the classical poet behind clue 10.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 10 makes Homer the poet, not the cartoon dad, until the cartoon arrives as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow father in The Simpsons is the best-known cartoon figure on television.

clue.text: Somewhere in Washington, elite national representative hacked

indicators.note: hacked means chopped off, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an Olympian is a top athlete chosen to represent a country

explanation.surface: A top sportsman representing the nation gets cut, somewhere in the American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington here is the state, not the city; its capital is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the state capital of Washington state in the north-west USA.

clue.text: Lamb perhaps to try first

parts.note: to essay is to attempt or try
1ST is the short form of first, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone eager to have the first go at cooking lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb was an English writer famous for his Essays of Elia, so lamb is not meat here.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb is a classic example of an English writer of short prose essays.

clue.text: Heard lumberjack getting variety of milk

indicators.note: heard tells us to use how the word sounds when spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: a sawyer is someone who saws timber, a lumberjack

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a lumberjack was getting a new sort of milk.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent with no final R, sawyer sounds just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk made from soybeans is a common plant-based alternative to dairy.

clue.text: Stream major thrash music

parts.note: the Mersey is a major river in north-west England, on which Liverpool stands
to thrash is to beat

explanation.surface: A big river and a thrashing, read as a band's loud style of music.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests thrash metal; thrash is just a verb meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the 1960s pop style from Liverpool, the sound of the early Beatles.

clue.text: To anoint unending circle, hand suddenly appears

indicators.note: unending means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to salve is to anoint or smear with ointment
the letter O is round like a circle

explanation.surface: A mystical scene: anointing an endless circle makes a hand appear.
explanation.walkthrough: A hand is a round of applause, as in give them a big hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a sudden burst, including a burst of applause or cheering.

clue.text: Much fluorescent lighting elevated party foxtrot

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means raised, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: neon is the gas in glowing tube lighting
a do is a party
Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dance party under bright fluorescent lights.
explanation.walkthrough: Foxtrot looks like a dance at a party, but it is the radio code word for F.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a great amount or lots, as in no end of trouble.

clue.text: Provider of relief with mug and fresh water for writer

parts.note: john is American slang for a toilet, where one relieves oneself
a stein is a beer mug
a beck is a stream in northern England

explanation.surface: A writer is given a mug of fresh water to bring relief.
explanation.walkthrough: Relief here is the lavatory kind, not comfort for a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the American novelist who wrote The Grapes of Wrath and Of Mice and Men.

clue.text: Adverse Parliamentarian ruined heir's new land in Wales

indicators.note: adverse here means turned against, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: an MEP is a Member of the European Parliament
broke means financially ruined

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A hostile MP squanders an heir's estate in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignore the apostrophe: HEIRS rearranges to SHIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pembrokeshire is a county in south-west Wales, a region of land with its own coastline.

clue.text: Structure's primarily ignored, certainly, reviewing poem

indicators.note: the first letter is left out

parts.note: a body is a structure, as in the body of a building

indicators.note: reviewing suggests looking back, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: yes, certainly

explanation.surface: A critic reviewing a poem ignores its structure but approves.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S of Structure's is kept as a letter after B is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic about the long voyage home of Odysseus is one of the great classical poems.

clue.text: Experience again captivating Spain — a number should do this

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to relive is to experience again
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Reliving a Spanish trip, with a number expected to do something.
explanation.walkthrough: A number is not a figure but something that numbs, an anaesthetic, which eases pain.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaesthetic is meant to ease or take away pain, the job of a numbing drug.

clue.text: Note jolly Cockney that's anal retentive?

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H, saying happy (jolly) as 'appy

explanation.surface: A cheerful Cockney who turns out to be fussy and obsessive.
explanation.walkthrough: Anal retentive is a fussy person in the surface; here it is literally something that retains what comes from a baby's bottom. A Cockney is a working-class Londoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's diaper is designed to hold in what comes out of the bottom.

clue.text: Colour expert, part of a school possibly

parts.note: lemon is a pale yellow colour
a dab, or dab hand, is an expert

explanation.surface: An expert on colour working in a school.
explanation.walkthrough: School here is a school of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This flatfish swims in shoals, so one could be a member of a school of fish.

clue.text: With pounding heart, I'm shaking, getting discipline at school

indicators.note: pounding means battered, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a tic is an involuntary twitch or shaking

explanation.surface: A nervous pupil with a pounding heart, shaking before a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Maths with numbers is one of the basic subjects taught in school.

clue.text: Copy partners in bridge card game amid frantic rate

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so these pieces go inside the others
frantic suggests wild disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: North and South are partners at the bridge table
crib is short for cribbage, a card game

explanation.surface: Bridge partners copying each other while playing cards at a frantic pace.
explanation.definitionFit: To transcribe is to write out a copy of something.

clue.text: Trapped in Siberia (frozen locks)

indicators.note: trapped in shows the answer is held within these clue words

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in Siberia with frozen hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks is hair, not things that lock.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, bushy hairstyle, and locks are hair.

clue.text: Novelist's King Charles eating treat

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, King Charles in Latin
to handle someone is to treat or deal with them

explanation.surface: A novelist's King Charles spaniel is eating a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: King Charles looks like the dog breed; it is the royal cipher CR.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler was the American author of hardboiled detective fiction such as The Big Sleep.

clue.text: Sky maybe showing end of one-day game

parts.note: Sky is a British broadband company, an example of an internet service provider

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the hyphenated word one-day

explanation.surface: A broadcaster showing the end of a one-day cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky, a UK TV and broadband firm, suggests cricket on TV; here it is an internet provider.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the children's guessing game of naming something seen that begins with a given letter.

clue.text: Deciding contest, pistol initially firing

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter

parts.note: a lay-off is a dismissal, a firing from a job

explanation.surface: A shoot-out decided by who fires the pistol first.
explanation.walkthrough: Firing suggests the pistol shot; it means sacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A play-off is an extra match held to settle a tie or decide a winner.

clue.text: Mum encircles wood with runner, champ here

indicators.note: encircles means goes round, so the other piece sits inside

parts.note: keep mum means stay silent; SH is the call for silence
teak is a hardwood
a runner is a river; the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A mother puts wood around a champion runner.
explanation.walkthrough: Champ is a verb meaning chew noisily, not a champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant serving grilled beef is somewhere diners munch and chew.

clue.text: Reverse opinion about Dicky Hunt, writing agent

indicators.note: dicky means unsound or shaky, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: ink is the medium used for writing

explanation.surface: Someone changes their view of a man named Hunt, who is a literary agent.
explanation.walkthrough: Writing agent looks like a literary agent; it is the stuff that writes. Dicky is British slang for weak or faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: To unthink something is to retract or undo a thought you held.

clue.text: Serve, using shoulder power, succeeded

parts.note: to shoulder a burden is to bear it
arm can mean power or might, as in the long arm of the law
S is the genealogy abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A tennis player succeeds by serving with shoulder power.
explanation.walkthrough: Serve is military service, not tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry weapons as a soldier is to do military service.

clue.text: Motorists coming across problem island

indicators.note: the motoring group spans or comes across the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: the AA, the Automobile Association, is a British motorists' club
a rub is a difficulty, as in there's the rub

explanation.surface: Drivers come across a problem while touring an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Aruba is a Caribbean isle off the coast of Venezuela.

clue.text: Course with endless Mexican food time-consuming?

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the other piece is taken inside
endless means the final letter is removed

parts.note: a nacho is a Mexican tortilla chip snack

explanation.surface: A meal course of Mexican food that seems to take forever.
explanation.walkthrough: Course stands for of course; the answer is slang meaning naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Natch is informal shorthand for naturally, i.e. of course.

clue.text: Unaltered parsnips regularly selected

indicators.note: every other letter is selected, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Parsnips chosen at regular intervals and left untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold as is are left in their present state, without change.

clue.text: Game flirt snaring Romeo

indicators.note: snaring means trapping, so one piece is caught inside the other

parts.note: a coquet is a flirt
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A flirt plays at snaring a Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo is the radio code for R, not a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Croquet is a lawn sport played by hitting balls through hoops with mallets.

clue.text: Person sent to the front, essentially, carrying magazine?

indicators.note: essentially points at the core of the word, its letters without the first and last

parts.note: the answer's outer letters hold, or carry, The Oldie, a British magazine

explanation.surface: A soldier at the front carrying an ammunition magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The magazine is both the clip of bullets a soldier carries and The Oldie, a British magazine for older readers, held in the middle of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops in the army are the ones posted to the battlefront.

clue.text: Renowned Tudor coin aquatic inhabitant found on islands

indicators.note: found on means placed after, so this piece comes after the islands

parts.note: the franc was the coin of France
a drake is a male duck, a water bird

explanation.surface: A famous Tudor finds a coin and a duck on some islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan sea captain who sailed around the world.
